bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta report comments[0].content / staged source checkout / vulnerable-commit snapshots of drifted files / patch.diff / saved Stage 01 sanitizer trace
bug_description.normalized: The witnessed input is exactly five bytes `6c 7c 20 05 1d`. At `suite/fuzz/fuzz_disasm.c:42`, selector byte `0x6c` is passed to `get_platform_entry()`, which returns index `14` (`108 % 47`), and in the vulnerable commit snapshot `platforms[14] = { CS_ARCH_PPC, CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN, "PPC-64", "ppc64be" }`. `cs_open()` stores that arch/mode in the handle, and `cs_disasm()` receives the remaining four bytes `7c 20 05 1d`. On the PowerPC path, `MCInst mci` is stack-allocated; `MCInst_Init()` marks each operand slot invalid and resets `size` but leaves untouched `ImmVal` union bytes uninitialized. `getInstruction()` sees the big-endian mode bit, forms `insn = 0x7c20051d`, and the default `DecoderTable32` entry matches that word to `TBEGIN` with decoder recipe 71. Recipe 71 extracts one 1-bit immediate and calls `MCOperand_CreateImm0()` once, so only `MI->Operands[0]` is initialized. The generated `TBEGIN` printer then incorrectly executes `printU1ImmOperand(MI, 1, O)`. `printU1ImmOperand()` therefore fetches `MCInst_getOperand(MI, 1)->ImmVal` from the untouched stack slot and forwards that poisoned `Value` to `printUInt32()`, whose `if (val > HEX_THRESHOLD)` branch is the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value sink.

source.description: First project statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker-controlled input and creates the platform-dispatch state used by the vulnerable PowerPC path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact five-byte witness `6c 7c 20 05 1d`. This statement reads `Data[0] = 0x6c` and forwards that selector byte to `get_platform_entry()`; the next step computes `108 % 47 = 14`, which selects vulnerable-commit `platforms[14] = { CS_ARCH_PPC, CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN, "PPC-64", "ppc64be" }`.
source.note: Scored source step. It is the first project statement that materializes attacker-controlled selector state from the witness byte before the modulo helper and later `cs_open()` arch/mode assignment.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSAN origin only. The poisoned bytes live in the stack storage backing `mci.Operands[]`; the later invalid-slot read comes from this stack object, not from a heap allocation.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved MemorySanitizer report says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `mci` in the stack frame of `cs_disasm`. `MCInst_Init()` later marks operand slots invalid and resets `size`, but it never writes the `ImmVal` union for untouched slots.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `printUInt32()` branches on the poisoned `Value` that `printU1ImmOperand()` forwarded from the never-written second operand slot.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `SStream.c:177:6` with callers `printU1ImmOperand` and `printInstruction`.

root_cause.description: The generated `TBEGIN` printer asks for operand 1 even though decoder recipe 71 materializes only operand 0, so the print path reads a second slot that was never initialized.
root_cause.note: The staged fix removes `TBEGIN` from this case, prints it with `printU1ImmOperand(MI, 0, O)`, and rewrites the generated `OperandInfo249` metadata so the printer layout matches the single-immediate decode recipe.

parser_admitted.description: Because the selected mode has the big-endian bit but no QPX/SPE bits, `getInstruction()` reaches the default `DecoderTable32`, which accepts `0x7c20051d` as `TBEGIN` instead of failing.

printer_called.description: After successful decode, `cs_disasm()` invokes the architecture printer on the partially populated `MCInst`, reaching the generated `TBEGIN` printer case that requests operand 1.

evidence_limitations: The staged workspace checkout is not identical to the metadata commit: `git diff` against `57502b0ea05dad947dbec2497d1672983a6e25db` shows drift in `suite/fuzz/platform.c` and a large line-map change in `arch/PowerPC/PPCInstPrinter.c`. This GT grounds selector-to-platform facts to the vulnerable-commit snapshot and sink-side printer line anchors to the saved MSan trace plus the staged checkout lines that match it.

The saved MSan stack does not show an inlined `MCInst_getOperand` or `MCOperand_getImm` frame, so the invalid-slot load is reconstructed from `printU1ImmOperand`, `MCInst_Init`, and decoder recipe 71 in the staged source.

The staged artifacts expose generated `PPCGen*.inc` files but not the upstream TableGen `.td` files that produced them, so the root cause is anchored at the generated statements actually present on the vulnerable path.

coarse_trace.summary: The source statement at `fuzz_disasm.c:42` reads selector byte `0x6c`, `get_platform_entry()` maps it to index 14, and `cs_open()` stores the vulnerable PowerPC `CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN` handle before the remaining four bytes are passed to `cs_disasm()`.
Capstone allocates stack `MCInst mci`, initializes operand kinds and size but not untouched `ImmVal` union bytes, and wires the selected handle into `mci.csh`.
The big-endian PowerPC decoder materializes `7c 20 05 1d` as `0x7c20051d`, and `DecoderTable32` decodes that word as `TBEGIN` with recipe 71, which creates exactly one immediate operand at slot 0.
The generated `TBEGIN` printer incorrectly requests operand 1 even though only operand 0 was initialized, so the print path reads the untouched second slot.
The poisoned operand value reaches `printUInt32()`, and its comparison on `val` triggers the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value report.

fine_trace.note: Source step. This statement reads selector byte `0x6c` from the witness and passes it to `get_platform_entry()`, creating the platform-dispatch input that step 2 reduces to index 14.
The helper computes `0x6c % 47 = 14`, returning the selector value that chooses the vulnerable PowerPC `platforms[14]` entry.
Using `i = 14`, `cs_open()` stores `arch = CS_ARCH_PPC` and `mode = CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN` in the handle. That mode value is later read through `MI->csh->mode` in `getInstruction()`.

fine_trace.code: size_t count = cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, address, 0, &all_insn);
fine_trace.note: The same witness call passes the configured handle plus the remaining four bytes `7c 20 05 1d` into `cs_disasm()`. Those bytes become the PowerPC instruction word on the crashing path.

depends_on.via: handle configured for PPC big-endian mode

fine_trace.note: Allocates the stack-backed `MCInst` whose operand union storage later supplies the poisoned bytes. The saved MSan report attributes the origin to this stack allocation in `cs_disasm`.

Initialization marks each operand slot invalid and resets `size` to 0, but it never writes the `ImmVal` union. Any slot the decoder does not populate, including `Operands[1]`, keeps its stack garbage from step 5.
Copies the selected handle into the `MCInst`, so PowerPC `getInstruction()` later observes the PPC big-endian mode bits via `MI->csh->mode`.
The PowerPC decoder checks `MI->csh->mode` and takes the big-endian arm because step 3 stored `CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN`, which includes `CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN`, in the handle.
In that arm, the four instruction bytes from step 4 are combined as big-endian `insn = 0x7c20051d`.
With no QPX or SPE bits in the selected mode, `getInstruction()` falls through to `DecoderTable32`; that table matches `0x7c20051d` to `TBEGIN` and selects decoder recipe 71.

depends_on.via: mode lacks QPX/SPE and retains big-endian PPC path

fine_trace.note: Recipe 71 extracts one 1-bit field and invokes `MCOperand_CreateImm0()` exactly once. The `TBEGIN` decode therefore produces one immediate operand, not a second printed operand.
Because `MI->size` is still 0 from step 6, this single call writes only `Operands[0]` and increments `size` to 1. `Operands[1]` remains the invalid, never-written slot from steps 5-6.

fine_trace.code:
// TBEGIN, TEND, TSR, XSRQPI, XSRQPIX, XSRQPXP
printU1ImmOperand(MI, 1, O);
fine_trace.note: Root cause. In the generated `TBEGIN` printer case, `printInstruction()` asks `printU1ImmOperand` for operand 1 even though steps 11-12 materialized only operand 0. The staged patch moves `TBEGIN` to the operand-0 case and rewrites its generated operand metadata (`OperandInfo249`) accordingly.

fine_trace.code:
unsigned int Value = (unsigned int)MCOperand_getImm(MCInst_getOperand(MI, OpNo));
printUInt32(O, Value);
fine_trace.note: With `OpNo = 1`, `printU1ImmOperand()` retrieves `MCInst_getOperand(MI, 1)->ImmVal` from the untouched slot and then passes that `Value` to `printUInt32`. The saved MSan frame for this function is at line 461, the `printUInt32(O, Value)` call immediately after the load.
MSAN sink. `printUInt32()` branches on the poisoned `Value` from step 14, producing the saved `printUInt32 -> printU1ImmOperand -> printInstruction` crash stack.

allocation_context.note: The saved MSan report says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `mci` in the stack frame of `cs_disasm`; the exact declaration is `MCInst mci;` at line 796.

The saved stack is `printUInt32 -> printU1ImmOperand -> printInstruction -> cs_disasm`; the fine trace fills in the selector-byte dispatch in `fuzz_disasm.c`, the `cs_open` handle-mode assignment, the big-endian `getInstruction()` branch, and the `TBEGIN` decoder recipe that populate only operand 0 before that printer path runs.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. `printInstruction` passes `OpNo = 1`, `printU1ImmOperand` fetches `MCInst_getOperand(MI, 1)->ImmVal`, and `printUInt32` immediately branches on that poisoned `Value`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix removes `TBEGIN` from the `printU1ImmOperand(MI, 1, O)` printer case, adds it to the operand-0 case, and rewrites the generated `OperandInfo249` metadata so `TBEGIN` is described consistently with recipe 71's single immediate operand.

poc.trigger: Exact five-byte witness `6c 7c 20 05 1d`. Byte `0x6c` selects index 14 and the vulnerable PowerPC `CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN` handle; bytes `7c 20 05 1d` decode as `TBEGIN` and reach the bad `printU1ImmOperand(MI, 1, O)` path until MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` in `printUInt32`.

format.name: libFuzzer input: 1-byte platform selector + 4-byte PPC instruction
format.contract: Use the exact 5-byte witness `6c 7c 20 05 1d`. The first byte must remain `0x6c` so `get_platform_entry()` selects index 14 and `cs_open()` stores `CS_ARCH_PPC` with `CS_MODE_64 | CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN`; the remaining four bytes must remain `7c 20 05 1d` so `getInstruction()` materializes `0x7c20051d`, `DecoderTable32` selects `TBEGIN` recipe 71, and the generated printer later misreads operand 1. This GT does not generalize beyond that exact selector/instruction pair.
